thread:
Noah: hey team, Noah here — first week on runtime. i'm trying to build the runtime from source on my M1 laptop but the CI runner is an x86 machine with A100s. local build succeeds but the artifacts we push to CI fail at ptxas/arch stage with: 
```bash
ptxas fatal   : Ptx assembler, V14.1.0
ptxas fatal   : Unknown option '-march=sm_80'
```
Anyone have a simple checklist for cross-compiling GPU kernels / PTX bits so CI can link + load them?

Priya: welcome Noah :wave: quick notes — ptxas is part of the CUDA toolkit and the host ptxas version in the CI image needs to support the target arch (sm_80, sm_90, etc). Common pitfalls: (1) building PTX on mac (or any non-matching toolkit version) and shipping it, (2) embedding cubin/ptx compiled with an older ptxas into libs expecting newer arch flags, (3) using clang device-side compilation without matching nvptx target. Which Docker image/toolkit are you using locally vs CI?

Noah: locally I'm using the remote devcontainer which has CUDA headers only (we copy headers for building) but not ptxas. CI uses ghcr.io/redwood/infr-runtime:cuda12-ubuntu which has toolkit 12.2 and ptxas. I think I accidentally compiled device code with clang's nvptx backend on mac which produced PTX strings that CI's ptxas chokes on.

oscar: that fits. Two pragmatic options: (A) don't compile PTX locally on mac — compile device code into embedded PTX at CI time inside a x86 toolkit container, or (B) vendor a cross-ptx toolchain in the build stage (install nvptx-tools that match target). We usually run `make device` in the CI container to ensure ptxas/cubin are produced there. Also check that build flags don't pass host-specific -arch flags.

Noah: ok makes sense. Any quick command to verify the PTX/cubin arch compatibility?

Priya: yes — run `cuobjdump --list-elf <objfile>` or `cuobjdump -ptx -sass <libfile>` inside the CI image to see which sm versions are present. Another quick check: `strings <ptxfile> | grep sm_` or `readelf -sW <obj> | grep sm_` sometimes helps. On CI we add a lint step that runs `ptxas --version` and fails if the version is older than the minimum for our target.

Noah: tried `cuobjdump` inside CI image, shows only sm_50 in the compiled object — no sm_80. That explains ptxas error. So my clang-compiled PTX didn't include the sm_80 code. I'll switch to compiling device code in CI.

oscar: one more gotcha: if you embed PTX and rely on JIT compilation on device, the driver on the GPU must support the PTX ISA. We had a case where PTX generated by a newer toolkit relied on ISA features not present on older drivers and runtime JIT failed. So for stable builds, prefer precompiling cubins for targeted architectures using a known ptxas in CI.

build-bot: CI: suggested change — add a separate job `device-compile` that runs inside ghcr.io/redwood/infr-runtime:cuda12-ubuntu to generate cubins/ptx and fail early if ptxas reports unknown arch flags. Template: 
```bash
# in CI job running in x86 toolkit image
ptxas --version || exit 1
make -C device build || exit 1
cuobjdump --list-elf build/device_kernels.o | tee /tmp/obj.txt
if ! grep -q "sm_80\|sm_90" /tmp/obj.txt; then echo "ERROR: missing target arch in device object" >&2; exit 1; fi
```

Noah: perfect, that solves my day-0 confusion. i'll update my branch to defer device compile to CI and ping y'all if anything breaks. thanks for the fast help! :raised_hands:
